raw_segments.text: to die of old age is a death rare, extraordinary,
and singular, not to be exceeded.
And since we have exceeded the ordinary bounds, which is the just measure of life, we ought
not to expect to go much further. Having escaped so many precipices of death, whereinto we
have seen so many other men fall, we should acknowledge that so extraordinary a fortune
as that which has hitherto rescued us from those eminent perils, and kept us from death,
and kept us alive beyond the ordinary term of living, is not like to continue long.
